Let \(n=1987\) and \(k=45\). For each element \(e\), let \(r_e\) be the number of sets containing it.

Since every pair of sets intersects in exactly one element,
\[
\sum_e \binom{r_e}{2}=\binom{1987}{2}.
\]
By the de Bruijn–Erdős bound, if no element is common to all sets, then
\[
n\le k^2-k+1=45^2-45+1=1981.
\]
But \(1987>1981\), so some element is contained in all \(1987\) sets.

Thus every set consists of this common element plus \(44\) other elements. Since pairwise intersections have size exactly \(1\), those other elements cannot appear in more than one set. Therefore the union size is
\[
1+1987\cdot 44=1+87428=87429.
\]

\[
\boxed{87429}
\]
